clue.text: Palin, perhaps, is traveller in a club abroad

indicators.note: something abroad has wandered far from home, so these letters stray out of their printed order

blocks.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative on the road
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering salesman abroad finds himself in a nightclub with a famous American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin, governor of Alaska and 2008 vice-presidential candidate, is the example behind 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin is a member of the US conservative party, so she is one example of the type.

clue.text: Peer into part of castle lacking art or aid to vision?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word art must be removed from the castle part
the nobleman goes into the shortened castle part, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a rampart is the defensive wall of a castle
taken as written, the letters to remove
an earl is a member of the peerage

explanation.surface: Someone gazes into a bare castle wall, looking for something to help them see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning to look, which suits the vision theme, but it is the nobleman. The question mark flags that a rear lamp helps other road users see a vehicle rather than its driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The red light at the back of a car lets following drivers spot it in darkness, a loose but fair helper of sight.

clue.text: Drink held by chap in tavern

indicators.note: held by says the letters are gripped inside the following words, spanning their join

blocks.note: read straight across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A man in a pub is holding his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinta is British slang, from 'pint of', for a pint of milk, made famous by the old 'Drinka Pinta Milka Day' advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a pint measure of milk or beer, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Northern town taken with old PM largely restraining ambassador and leader of town to make peace

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the former premier loses a last letter
restraining means holding in, so the shortened name grips the diplomat inside it
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England
Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister 1979-90
HE, His or Her Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A northern town, a former prime minister and a diplomat come together to settle a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ambassador sits inside THATCHE(R) after its first letter, and the town's initial is tacked on after that, giving BURY THE HATCHET.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a Native American custom of burying weapons, means to end a quarrel and become reconciled.

clue.text: Assistant has first put down plan

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting the first letter down sends it to the bottom, the end of the word

blocks.note: an aide is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A helper lays down a scheme before anyone else does.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme thought up in advance is an idea, a common synonym for intention.

clue.text: Mother introducing juice quietly amid beer — such is moved during drinking?

indicators.note: introducing means bringing on next, so the parent is followed directly by the juice
amid means in the middle of, so the earlier letters sit inside the beer

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
sap is the juice of a plant
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A mother adds juice to her beer as she drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' and 'beer' set a drinking scene, but the whole final phrase is the definition: the lump in the throat bobs up and down as you swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The projection of the larynx in the throat visibly rises and falls with every swallow, which is what the cryptic hint describes.

clue.text: Exchange in prisoners recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captives are brought home as part of a prisoner exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Swop is a variant spelling of swap, to trade one thing for another, so it means barter.

clue.text: Pin that’s not genuine?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fake fastening pin or brooch
setter's reading: pin is slang for a leg, and a false one is a carved replacement limb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins' is informal British for legs; a false leg made from timber is the classic pirate's prosthesis.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial limb carved from timber replaces a lost leg, so it is a fake version of a pin in slang.

clue.text: Artist is engaged in exercise to get approval

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied inside, so the earlier words sit within the exercise

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a common crossword artist
taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A painter who works out in the gym hopes to win admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is expressed admiration or commendation, a close synonym for approbation.

clue.text: Nominal minister improvised a solo civic part

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so the letters are put together freshly

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman ad-libs a solo role in a civic ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A vicar apostolic is a Catholic bishop who holds the title of a defunct see while governing a mission territory, hence 'nominal'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman Catholic cleric is a titular bishop, holding his rank in name of an extinct diocese, so a minister in title only.

clue.text: Course popular when entering a service, say

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the word for popular goes into the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
the service tree is a European tree related to the rowan, so it is an example of the general word
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Something goes down well when it becomes part of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship or tennis, but the service tree is a real species of Sorbus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.

clue.text: Number touring limited region? Hot region

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the song goes around the next part
limited means cut short, so the region word loses its last letter

blocks.note: an aria is a musical number, a song in an opera
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: A touring act visits a small area, then a sweltering one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but it is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-western US state is famous for its desert climate, so it is a sweltering area.

clue.text: Six-footer staying in house and shed

indicators.note: staying in means remaining inside, so the creature sits within the house

blocks.note: an ant is an insect, which has six legs or feet
Leo is one of the twelve houses or signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A very tall person stays home and in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is any insect. A house in astrology is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding whose roof rests against a wall, a kind of shed.

clue.text: Witness step to restrict inmates lately being withdrawn — these might result?

indicators.note: lately points to the latest part, the final letter of the word
to restrict means to hold in, so the stride holds the letter inside it
withdrawn means pulled back, so the whole assembly is read backwards

blocks.note: to see is to witness
a pace is a step
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A witness steps forward to keep prisoners from being released.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: if inmates are 'withdrawn' from prison, fugitives result.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners who have got out of jail are what you get when inmates leave without permission, so they are the outcome.

clue.text: Dish in sound oven chef initially made to be large

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word
made to be means turned into, so one letter is replaced by another

blocks.note: sound means good, in reliable condition
a cooker is a stove or oven
the first letter of the word
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes sizes

explanation.surface: A chef puts a dish into an oven and turns it up high.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'Dish' look like food; it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal for a very attractive person, and a good-looker is exactly that.

clue.text: Shell might include this sort of a home for petrol, nothing less

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant form, so these letters are rearranged
less means minus, so one letter is taken away from the fodder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Shell, the oil company, might own a sort of home for petrol, a filling station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' and 'petrol' conjure the oil company; the shell is a mollusc's, lined with nacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, the iridescent lining of oyster and mussel shells, is a material found inside such casings.

clue.text: Vulgar woman harbouring terrible tales

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the word that follows is badly mangled
harbouring means sheltering inside, so the woman holds the rest within her

blocks.note: Tess is a woman's name
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A coarse woman keeps dreadful stories to herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking refinement or good judgement, crude and in poor style, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Neat American managed boat

blocks.note: trim means neat and tidy
A is the abbreviation for American
ran means managed, as a business

explanation.surface: A tidy American ran a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a vessel with three parallel hulls, so it is a type of sailing craft.

clue.text: Study look about male in peril — origin of hurtful gossip?

indicators.note: about means around, so the look word goes around the man
in places the preceding letters inside the word for peril

blocks.note: to scan is to study closely
lo is an old word meaning look
M is the abbreviation for male
danger means peril

explanation.surface: Someone studies a man in danger, wondering what started the cruel rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: L(M)O goes inside DANGER after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads malicious rumours about others is where wounding tittle-tattle comes from.

clue.text: Singular set of beliefs found in long passage

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
a creed is a system of religious belief

explanation.surface: A unique set of beliefs is laid out in a lengthy piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a lengthy, often tedious, piece of writing, so it is an extended text.

clue.text: Top reptile imbued with energy coming back in force

indicators.note: imbued with means filled with, so the reptile has the energy letter inside it
coming back means returning, so the whole assembly is read backwards

blocks.note: No 1, number one, is the top, written as NO and I
croc is short for crocodile
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A superb reptile, full of energy, comes back in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' must be read as No 1, with the numeral as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion is compulsion by threats or violence, the use of power to make someone comply.

clue.text: Trail group of students

blocks.note: first meaning: to flow or float out behind, as hair or a banner does
second meaning: a class of pupils grouped by ability in a British school

explanation.walkthrough: Streaming in British schools means sorting pupils into ability classes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to float out behind, and as a noun it is a school class of similar ability.

clue.text: Reveal excessive feeling in book on iPad that’s brought up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means lifted from bottom to top, so read backwards

blocks.note: a book read on a tablet is an electronic volume, an e-tome

explanation.surface: Someone gets overemotional over a book they are reading on a tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion theatrically or exaggeratedly, as an actor might.

clue.text: Touch instrument in turn

indicators.note: in turn suggests turning round, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone touches each instrument one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut share a boundary and are in contact, so the verb means to adjoin.

clue.text: Condition of horse in brass behind tree, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be taken as it is spoken, not as written
behind sets the first piece after the tree word

blocks.note: a yew is an evergreen tree, and it is pronounced like the word for a female sheep
brass and neck both mean cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A horse's condition is shown in a brass plaque behind a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' and 'neck' are both British slang for impudence. A ewe-neck is a horse's neck that arches the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe-neck is a conformation fault in horses, a thin neck with a concave top line.

clue.text: Old PM, figure behind revolutionary scientific establishment

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests revolving, turning over, so the establishment word is read backwards
behind puts the number after the turned establishment word

blocks.note: a lab, laboratory, is a scientific establishment
four is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is behind a radical science institute.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was the British Conservative prime minister from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: Daughter facing river in twilight

indicators.note: facing means in front of, so the daughter comes before the river

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the Usk is a river in south Wales

explanation.surface: A daughter looks out over a river at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the darker stage of evening twilight, just before nightfall, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Cretin with cart unsettled bird

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed from its place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letters to be rearranged
the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool with a cart disturbs a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic tern is a seabird famous for the longest migration of any animal.
